battle.name: 侯景叛梁魏之戰
battle.brief: 太清二年十月侯景於寒山舉兵，捨壽陽而東，自橫江以騎數百、步八千渡江，奪采石、克姑孰，直逼建康。蕭正德開宣陽門迎之，侯景圍臺城逾百日，梁武帝餓死其間。承聖元年陳霸先夜襲渇浦、王僧辯進兵，侯景兵敗被部將所殺。卡面科林斯青銅盔是對照件：本役靠撞車、飛梯與舟船取城，與全封閉面甲無涉。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 侯景叛梁魏之戰表面上是兩個政權的對抗，實際上捲入南梁朝廷、侯景叛軍、北齊與西魏四股力量，而戰場重心始終在建康臺城。南梁一方以梁武帝蕭衍坐鎮建康中樞，軍事上靠禁軍宿衛與揚、徐、豫三州州鎮兵分頭擔任：蕭衍以邵陵王蕭倫總督諸軍征討，以羊侃由廣州刺史改任采石戍主守江防，以平北將軍蕭正德都督京師諸軍事、屯丹陽郡，另遣王質率水軍三千巡弋長江，郡守如臨川太守陳昕、淮南太守蕭寧各以本州兵當敵。侯景一方是原東魏河南行台的班底，核心為北鎮降戶與河南州郡部曲，騎兵見長，兵眾號稱十餘萬而史書多記為數萬至十二萬不等，分作三路：王偉等謀主與行台官屬在軍中掌文書符令，前鋒輕騎自歷陽、姑孰一路掃清渡口，主力則攜撞車、飛梯、鉤車等攻城器械乘舟溯流而上，另留王顯貴守壽陽作後方。背景中的北齊由高洋接位，殺死侯景留在北方的子女，又按兵觀望；西魏趁梁室內鬥招撫宗室，蕭詧以襄陽降魏、蕭綸投齊，梁王封號都成了北方插手南朝的支點。荊州的蕭繹與益州的蕭紀各擁兵自守，號稱勤王而實按兵不動，荊州兵直到後期才成為平叛主力。
countriesEn: On the surface the war of Hou Jing's revolt against Liang was a clash between two polities, but in fact four forces were involved: the Liang court, Hou Jing's rebel army, Northern Qi and Western Wei, and the centre of gravity of the fighting remained the palace city of Jiankang. The Liang side was Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan, holding the central secretariat at Jiankang, with the fighting carried by the imperial guard and the provincial troops of Yang, Xu and Yu: Xiao Yan sent the Prince of Shaoling, Xiao Lun, to command the punitive expedition, made Yang Kan, promoted from governor of Guang prefecture, commander of the Caishi garrison to hold the river crossing, appointed the Prince of Pingbei, Xiao Zhengde, as commander of all the armies of the capital and quartered him at Danyang, and further sent Wang Zhi with three thousand naval troops to patrol the river, while commandery governors such as Chen Xin, governor of Linchuan, and Xiao Ning, governor of Huainan, met the enemy with the troops of their own prefectures. Hou Jing's side was the cadre of his old office as Director of Henan Circuit under Eastern Wei, its core the surrendered households of the northern garrisons and the local contingents of the Henan commanderies, strong in cavalry; his host was proclaimed at more than a hundred thousand men while the histories give figures from several tens of thousands to a hundred and twenty thousand, and it was divided into three parts: Wang Wei and the other advisers and clerical officials of the staff directing documents and orders in the camp, a vanguard of light horse clearing the crossings along the line from Liyang through Gushu, and the main body carrying rams, scaling ladders and hooked poles, which came up the river in boats; a third detachment under Wang Xiangui was left to hold Shouyang as the rear. In the background, Northern Qi under Gao Yang had just succeeded to the throne, killed the sons Hou Jing had left in the north, and watched from the sidelines; Western Wei took advantage of the fighting inside the Liang house to win over members of the imperial clan, with Xiao Chen surrendering Xiangyang to Wei and Xiao纶 defecting to Qi, the title of Prince of Liang becoming in both cases the hinge on which the northern courts meddled in the south. In Jingzhou, Xiao Yi, and in Yizhou, Xiao Ji, each held troops where they stood, professing to rally to the cause while in fact keeping their men to themselves, and only the Jingzhou army became the main instrument of the suppression in the later stages.
people: 推動這場戰爭的有三股人。侯景字萬卿，懷朔鎮出身，父侯瑒為魏鎮將，死於葛榮之亂；他先隸爾朱榮，後歸高歡，尚高歡女兒，官至河南行台。548年舉兵時他已六十餘歲，自寒山聚眾數千，因糧食不給而連夜南行，渡江之後兵力迅速膨脹，進逼建康時已打算自己稱帝；入城之後逼蕭衍遜位，以王偉為謀主，偽造祖宗譜系、稱漢朝侯霸為始祖，自立為漢帝，改元太始。梁武帝蕭衍是這場災難的另一個核心：他兩度遣使求援卻把指揮權交給各路宗室，自己退守淨居殿，最後在侯景克扣飲食之下餓死。羊侃是全場最關鍵的守將，他曾建議先以二千人守采石、另分一軍攻壽陽，因朱異反對未行，侯景渡江之後他退守臺城，築樓架弩、掘地道反擊、折撞車破飛梯，圍城百餘日幾乎全靠他一人撐住，至太清三年十一月病卒，臺城人心隨之崩解。蕭正德是最關鍵的內應，侯景兵抵朱雀桁時由他開宣陽門迎入，後又圖謀刺殺侯景，事敗被殺。平叛的兩位主角是陳霸先與王僧辯：前者以精兵夜襲渇浦，後者自荊州引兵東下；侯景敗後企圖乘舟突圍，被部將羊鵾所殺，一說病歿舟中。宗室蕭繹因平亂有功而入繼大統，蕭詧、蕭紀卻各自覬覦，一個降西魏、一個據益州，最終把梁朝推向覆亡。
peopleEn: Three groups of men drove this war forward. Hou Jing, courtesy name Wanqing, came from the Huixuo garrison; his father Hou Yang had been a commander in Wei and was killed in the rebellion of Ge Rong. He first served under Erzhu Rong, then attached himself to Gao Huan and married one of Gao Huan's daughters, rising to the office of Director of Henan Circuit. When he rose in 548 he was already past sixty, gathering only a few thousand men at Hanshan and marching south by night because he had no grain; once across the river his numbers swelled rapidly, and by the time he stood before Jiankang he had already settled on claiming the imperial title for himself. After he entered the city he forced Xiao Yan to abdicate, took Wang Wei as his chief adviser, fabricated a genealogy that traced his line to the Han founder Hou Ba, proclaimed himself emperor of Han and changed the era to Taishi. Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan, was the other core of the catastrophe: he called up reinforcements twice yet handed the command to scattered members of the imperial clan, retired to the Jingju hall and died of starvation when Hou Jing cut his food. Yang Kan was the most important defending general of the whole war. He had proposed holding Caishi with two thousand men while another force struck at Shouyang, but the advice was rejected by Zhu Yi; after Hou Jing crossed the river he fell back on the palace city, raised towers, mounted crossbows, dug tunnels out to strike at the besiegers, broke the rams and the scaling ladders, and for the best part of a hundred days of siege it was he alone who held the place together, until he died of illness in the eleventh month of the third year of Taiqing and the defenders' nerve went with him. Xiao Zhengde was the most important man inside the city: when Hou Jing's army reached the Zhuque Bridge it was he who opened the Xuanyang Gate to admit it, and later he plotted to kill Hou Jing and was killed himself when the plot was uncovered. The two heroes of the counter-offensive were Chen Baxian and Wang Sengbian, the former striking Gupu by night with picked troops, the latter bringing the Jingzhou army east; after his defeat Hou Jing tried to break out by boat and was killed by his own commander Yang Kun, though one account has him dying of illness in his boat. Among the imperial clan, Xiao Yi entered the succession on the credit of putting down the rebellion, while Xiao Chen and Xiao Ji each schemed for themselves, one surrendering to Western Wei, the other holding Yizhou, and in the end they pushed the Liang house towards its destruction.
kits: 卡面是科林斯青銅盔，Corinthian helmet，公元前七世紀的希臘青銅器，全正面開眼，只在鼻樑兩側留出狹長的目孔，連下顎都包住。它從未在中國出土，也沒有出現在任何一支中國軍隊的裝備序列裡，在本役中的角色是對照件：全封閉的面甲能把頭部護得嚴實，代價是視野與聽覺都被壓到最低，戴它的人只能靠隊形與口令活命。南朝真正配在頭上的是兜鍪，以漆皮或鐵葉為主，配護頰與獸吞護肩，兩當鎧常用白紗與皂紗，具裝騎兵另有鐵質人甲與馬鎧，馬具已用鐵馬鐙與勒具；步卒多不著甲，兵器以槊、矛、戟、長刀為主，弓弩分蹶張弓、腰弩與床弩，箭用竹矢，配小盾或圓盾。攻城一側的裝備才是本役的主角：撞車、飛梯即巢車、鉤車、發石車與土山、木城，配合火箭與鹿角、鐵蒺藜；守方以擂石、床弩、檑木與城頭木樓回應，羊侃並在城內掘地道通到城外反擊。運輸上侯景靠的是船，舟艦既載兵也載攻城器械與糧秣，這正是他敢於忽視陸路補給的底氣。兩相比較之下，這場戰爭的勝負從來不靠個人護甲，而靠器械、糧秣與隊形。
kitsEn: The card shows a Corinthian helmet, a Greek bronze piece of the seventh century BC with the face fully enclosed and only a narrow eye opening left on either side of the nasal, the jaw covered as well. It has never been found in China and appears in no Chinese army's inventory; in this war its role is that of a reference piece. A fully closed face plate protects the head thoroughly, at the price of cutting field of view and hearing down to the minimum, so that the man wearing it can only stay alive by the discipline of his formation and by word of command. What was actually worn on the head in the Southern dynasties was the doumou, made of lacquered leather or iron plates, fitted with cheek pieces and a shoulder guard shaped like a beast's head; the liangdang armour was commonly faced in white or black gauze; armoured riders had iron cuirasses and caparisons for the horse, with iron stirrups and better harness. Most infantry fought unarmoured, carrying the spear, the long lance, the ji halberd and the long sword, with the bow and crossbow divided between the strong recurved bow, the waist crossbow and the bed crossbow, using bamboo shafts for arrows and carrying small or round shields. On the siege side the equipment is what dominates this war: battering rams, scaling ladders in the form of the nest-cart, hooked poles, stone-throwing engines, earthen mounds and timber works, backed by fire arrows and by caltrops and iron spikes. The defenders answered with dropped stones, bed crossbows, raking poles and wooden towers on the walls, and Yang Kan dug tunnels inside the walls that came out beyond the city to strike at the besiegers. In transport Hou Jing relied on boats: hulls carried men, siege machines and grain alike, and that is precisely why he could afford to ignore supply by land. Set side by side, the two sides of this war make the point that the outcome was never decided by individual armour but by machines, supply and formation.
tactics: 侯景起手三步，都是省力的打法。第一步是捨棄淮南：九月他放棄壽陽，詐稱出城遊獵，實則把主力拉回江邊，十月又揚言進攻合肥，實取譙州、歷陽，把真實進攻方向藏在謠言裡。第二步是抓換防的空隙：采石守軍王質與陳昕換防之間，侯景以騎數百人配合步兵八千人自橫江夜渡，一鼓奪采石，俘陳昕，再分兵取姑孰、俘淮南太守蕭寧，進至慈湖。第三步是內應開門：兵抵朱雀桁，蕭正德開宣陽門迎其入城。圍城之後，他把營壘與器械分隊配置：撞車對城門與土山，飛梯與鉤車對城頭，發石車壓制城上守卒，器械隊與突擊隊輪番上列、白晝不絕，同時在營旁築山築壘逼近城牆，把臺城西面封成一片攻城陣地。守方是另一套邏輯：羊侃在城頭築樓，備擂石、弓弩與檑木，以撞擊折斷飛梯、擊碎撞車，又掘地道繞到城外反擊，使進攻方的器械隊與突擊隊無法同時展開。但援軍失期改變了一切：蕭倫統率的援軍雖號稱百萬，實則多為各地響應之眾，糧秣不繼且指揮不統一，侯景得以集中兵力反覆打散；後期侯景又把主力分兵西進江州、豫章、湘州，使建康一線空虛，陳霸先、王僧辯才得以聯軍東下，最後以夜襲渇浦切斷退路，一夜之間把攻守之勢倒過來。
tacticsEn: Hou Jing's opening moves were all ways of saving effort. The first was to abandon Huainan: in the ninth month he gave up Shouyang under the pretext of going hunting outside the walls, actually drawing his main body back to the river, and in the tenth month he threatened to attack Hefei while really taking Qiaozhou and Liyang, hiding his true line of advance inside rumour. The second was to seize the gap left by a change of garrison: while the Caishi troops of Wang Zhi and Chen Xin were changing over, he crossed the river by night from Hengjiang with several hundred horsemen and eight thousand foot, took Caishi in one stroke, captured Chen Xin, then sent a detachment against Gushu, took the governor of Huainan, Xiao Ning, captive and came on to Cihu. The third was to have the gate opened from within: the army reached the Zhuque Bridge and Xiao Zhengde threw open the Xuanyang Gate to admit it. Once the siege began, he distributed his works and his troops by task: rams against the gates and against his own earthen mounds, scaling ladders and hooked poles against the walls, stone-throwing engines to keep down the defenders on the parapets, engine crews and storming parties drawn up side by side and taking turns, hammering day and night, while he raised mounds and works beside his camp to close the distance, sealing the western side of the palace city into one continuous attacking position. The defenders followed a different logic. Yang Kan raised towers on the walls, stocked them with dropped stones, bows and raking poles, used the impact of heavy weights to break the ladders and shatter the rams, and dug tunnels that came out beyond the walls so that the engine crews and the storming parties could never deploy at the same time. But the failure of the relief armies changed everything. The force under Xiao Lun was proclaimed at a hundred thousand, yet in truth it consisted mostly of contingents answering the call from all over, without a common command and without a common supply line, and Hou Jing was able to concentrate and break it again and again. Later he split his main force westwards into Jiangzhou, Yuzhang and Xiangzhou, leaving the Jiankang line thin; only then could Chen Baxian and Wang Sengbian bring their combined army east, and the night attack on Gupu cut the way back, turning the tide of attack and defence over in a single night.
data: 留下數字的地方不少，但多出自勝方與後世史家的約數。兵員方面，侯景起兵時所部只有數千，渡江之後旬日之間膨脹到數萬，《梁書》與《資治通鑑》所記「眾號百萬」多為各路響應之兵，別一說法記其為九萬至十二萬；蕭倫率領的援軍同樣號稱百萬，前線實際投入以萬計。渡江那一夜的投入是本役最清楚的一組數：以騎數百人配合步兵八千人奪采石。守城方面，臺城被圍之初可戰之兵有披甲者二萬餘人，圍城百餘日之後據載只剩二三千人守在城頭，多半帶傷。時間線上，548年十月舉兵，同年冬渡江，太清三年三月圍臺城，同年十一月羊侃病卒，十二月城破，549年五月蕭衍死，550年侯景自建康出兵西征三吳，552年三月陳霸先夜襲渇浦，侯景自550年自立至552年敗亡，在位不到兩年。距離上，采石至建康江行約六十餘公里，合一百二十里上下，器械與糧秣靠船一日可達；侯景的舟隊則是自采石、姑孰一路溯流直抵京口一線的宮城之下，器械與人馬同船而至，不需在陸上轉運。
dataEn: Numbers survive in fair quantity, though most are the rough estimates of the victors and of later historians. On strength, the troops Hou Jing had with him when he rose numbered only a few thousand and swelled to several tens of thousands within a fortnight of the crossing; the hundred thousand recorded in the History of Liang and in the Comprehensive Mirror count mostly contingents answering the call from all over, while another reckoning gives his force as between ninety thousand and a hundred and twenty thousand. The relief army under Xiao Lun was likewise proclaimed at a hundred thousand, while what was actually committed to the front line was counted in tens of thousands. The clearest single set of figures belongs to the night of the crossing: several hundred horsemen and eight thousand foot were enough to take Caishi. On the defensive side, the palace city at the beginning of the siege had more than twenty thousand men in armour available, and after a hundred days or more of siege the records say only two or three thousand men were still on the walls, most of them wounded. The chronology runs: the rising in the tenth month of 548, the crossing of the river in the same winter, the investment of the palace city in the third month of the third year of Taiqing, the death of Yang Kan in the eleventh month of the same year, the fall of the city in the twelfth month, the death of Xiao Yan in the fifth month of 549, Hou Jing's westward campaign into the Three Wu in 550, and Chen Baxian's night attack on Gupu in the third month of 552; between his proclamation as emperor in 550 and his defeat in 552 his reign lasted less than two years. In distance, the run of the river from Caishi to Jiankang is a little over sixty kilometres, some hundred and twenty li, and both machines and grain could be carried a day's sail at a time. Hou Jing's flotillas went straight up the river from Caishi and Gushu to the palace city below Jingkou, machines and men arriving in the same hulls with no need to shift anything overland.
cause: 起兵有直接導火線，也有更深的體制原因。導火線是一樁人質交易：太清元年侯景降梁，梁朝默許他割據壽陽、封為河南王；其後貞陽侯蕭淵明被東魏俘虜，侯景偽造東魏書信與梁武帝約定以蕭淵明換回自己，蕭衍竟然答應。侯景聞之大怒——一個能被交出去的河南王，等於被朝廷判了死刑，於是太清二年十月在寒山舉兵，豫、譙等州郡多響應。體制原因在梁朝這一邊：蕭衍中晚年篤信佛教，軍國大事多倚朱異等佞臣，禁軍宿衛久廢，州鎮兵調發無常，采石這樣的咽喉要地只以少量兵力輪守；羊侃提議以二千人守采石並分兵斷壽陽，理由充分卻被朱異駁回，江防的漏洞就這樣留了下來。侯景自身的處境也逼他孤注一擲：他雖有河南行台的兵權，卻得不到北朝朝廷的信任，留在北方只會被清算，南下又無合法名分，唯一能拿出的本錢是河南饑民與降戶組成的軍隊，糧食不給時只能靠冒險換取地盤。於是548年的寒山一點火，這場戰爭就從淮南燒到建康，再由建康燒到荊州與益州。
causeEn: The rising had an immediate trigger as well as deeper structural causes. The trigger was a bargain over a hostage. In the first year of Taiqing Hou Jing submitted to Liang, and the Liang court tacitly allowed him to hold Shouyang and made him Prince of Henan; later the Prince of Zhenyang, Xiao Yuanming, was captured by Eastern Wei, and Hou Jing forged a letter from Eastern Wei to propose to Xiao Yan that Yuanming be exchanged for him, and Xiao Yan actually agreed. Hou Jing was furious at this: a Prince of Henan who could be traded away had been sentenced to death by the court, and so in the tenth month of the second year of Taiqing he raised his banner at Hanshan, and the commanderies of Yu and Qiao answered the call. The structural cause lay on the Liang side. In his later years Xiao Yan was engrossed in Buddhism, the business of state and war was left to favourites such as Zhu Yi, the imperial guard had long gone slack, and provincial troops were called out without regularity; a vital crossing like Caishi was held by only a small rotating force. Yang Kan's proposal to station two thousand men at Caishi while another force cut Shouyang was sound in every particular and was turned down by Zhu Yi, and the gap in the river defence was left standing. Hou Jing's own position drove him to stake everything. He held the authority of Henan Circuit but enjoyed no trust from the northern court, and to stay in the north meant eventual liquidation, while going south gave him no lawful standing; the only capital he could offer was an army drawn from hungry men and surrendered households in Henan, and with no grain in hand the only move left was to risk everything in exchange for ground. One spark at Hanshan in 548, and the war burned from Huainan to Jiankang, and from Jiankang on to Jingzhou and Yizhou.
impact: 這場戰爭改變的不只是梁一朝。短期看，梁朝中央的軍事體系被打散：禁軍宿將三年之內或死或降，宿衛建康的部隊幾乎被侯景收編，圍城百餘日之後，能成建制重組的只剩下荊州方面帶回來的兵與收撫的降卒，王僧辯與陳霸先正是靠這批力量在數年之內問鼎帝位。中期看，宗室內鬥把北方勢力直接拉了下來：蕭詧以襄陽降西魏、蕭綸投北齊、蕭紀據益州，蕭繹雖平了侯景，兩年之後江陵仍為西魏所破，梁元帝遇害，南朝長江中游的門戶洞開。長期看，南朝由梁入陳再入隋的軌道就此鋪成：士族在兵禍與宗室互相傾軋中被消耗，軍權落到陳霸先手上，557年陳代梁，589年隋平陳。軍備層面的教訓最為直接——重兵在邊而禁軍空虛，一旦被侯景這樣的人抓住，整個王朝都沒有縱深可撐；而全正面封閉的頭盔從來不是南方軍隊的答案，這場戰役真正起作用的是器械、舟船與糧秣。
impactEn: This war changed far more than the single Liang house. In the short term the military structure of the Liang centre was broken apart: within three years the commanders of the imperial guards were killed or surrendered, the troops that garrisoned Jiankang were almost entirely absorbed into Hou Jing's army, and after a hundred days of siege the only forces that could be reconstituted as units were the men brought back by the Jingzhou army and the surrendered stragglers who were rounded up; Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian were able to bid for the throne within a few years precisely on the strength of these. In the medium term the fighting between members of the imperial clan dragged the northern powers in directly: Xiao Chen surrendered Xiangyang to Western Wei, Xiao Lun fled to Northern Qi, Xiao Ji held Yizhou, and although Xiao Yi put down Hou Jing, Jiangling fell to Western Wei two years later and the Emperor Yuan of Liang was taken; the gate on the middle Yangtze stood open. In the long term the road from Liang to Chen and on to Sui was laid: the aristocratic clans were consumed by war and by their own internecine quarrels, military power passed to Chen Baxian, the Chen replaced the Liang in 557 and the Sui conquered the south in 589. The most direct lesson was one of armament: with the heavy troops on the frontier and the imperial guard hollow, once a man like Hou Jing took hold of that weakness, the dynasty had no depth left to absorb the blow. And a fully closed face plate was never the answer for a southern army: what decided this war was machines, boats and grain.
result: 結果是叛軍覆滅，但代價極大。承聖元年三月，陳霸先以精兵夜襲渇浦得手，侯景大軍當即崩潰，退保建康一線；他企圖乘舟突圍，部將羊鵾不從，遂殺之，一說侯景病歿舟中，年六十七歲。他自立的漢只存在不到兩年，從未得到任何一州一郡的正式承認；王僧辯隨即迎立太子蕭綱，是為簡文帝，改元承聖，廢黜蕭棟；侯景的頭顱送到江陵，雙手送交北齊高洋，屍骨被焚。荊州軍接管建康之後，侯景殘部多被收編，攻城器械與繳獲的甲兵散落江表，其中一部分後來成了陳霸先整編軍備的來源。戰爭的尾巴一直拖到554年：江陵陷落，梁元帝蕭繹被西魏所擒，益州先失於西魏，南朝失去上游屏障；554年王僧辯被陳霸先所殺，557年陳霸先代梁建陳。就軍事史而言，侯景叛梁魏之戰是南朝記載最完整的攻城戰之一，圍城百餘日的攻防、舟船運器械、夜襲渡口等細節都留了下來；就政治而言，它證明了一個王朝可以在四年之間被一支缺糧的偏師從邊鎮一路打到首都。
resultEn: The rebels were destroyed, but the cost was enormous. In the third month of the first year of Chengsheng, Chen Baxian struck Gupu by night with picked troops and succeeded, and Hou Jing's main army broke at once and fell back on the Jiankang line. He tried to break out by boat; his commander Yang Kun would not allow it and killed him, though one account has Hou Jing dying of illness in his boat at the age of sixty-seven. The Han he had proclaimed lasted less than two years and was never acknowledged by a single prefecture or commandery. Wang Sengbian then brought the crown prince Xiao Gang forward as Emperor Jianwen, changed the era to Chengsheng and deposed Xiao Dong. Hou Jing's head was sent to Jiangling, his hands to the Northern Qi emperor Gao Yang, and his body was burned. Once the Jingzhou army took over Jiankang, most of Hou Jing's remnant was absorbed, and the siege machines and captured armour lay scattered across the Jiang region, some of it later serving as one of the sources for Chen Baxian's rearmament. The tail of the war dragged on to 554: Jiangling fell, the Emperor Yuan of Liang, Xiao Yi, was taken by Western Wei, Yizhou had already been lost to the same court, and the southern dynasty lost its upper barrier on the river. In 554 Wang Sengbian was killed by Chen Baxian, and in 557 Chen Baxian replaced the Liang and founded the Chen. In terms of military history, the war of Hou Jing's revolt is among the most completely recorded sieges of the Southern dynasties, with the hundred days of attack and defence, the carriage of machines by boat and the night assault on the crossing all preserved in the record. In terms of politics, it proved that a dynasty can be carried from its frontier garrison to its capital in four years by a hungry detachment of troops.
